ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier, CMF); Article L561-46 CMF and Decree No. 2016-1423 of 24 October 2016 (declaration of beneficial owners to the Registre National des Entreprises); Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Articles L562-1 et seq. CMF (asset freezing and counter-sanctions); Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (Fifth Anti-Money Laundering Directive).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (certificat d'existence / certificate of non-insolvency) of each non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or trade register of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) OR French Consular Legalization for non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the articles of association / by-laws of each non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution (board or shareholders) authorizing the incorporation of the French SAS and the appointment of its President
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Governing body of the non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney in favor of the French incorporating representative / avocat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin (or a French notaire where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport or national identity card of each natural-person UBO, with proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State authority and utility/service provider in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy; apostille not required where certified by counsel; French sworn translation mandatory

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of the SAS President, members of corporate governing bodies, every shareholder holding 25% or more of capital or voting rights, and all UBOs against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the French national asset-freezing measures under Articles L562-1 et seq. CMF (administered by the Ministry for the Economy and Finance), and (iv) OFAC SDN and related lists as an extra-territorial best-practice layer. PEP status is assessed on a risk-adjusted basis in accordance with FATF guidance and Article L561-10 CMF; any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence and, where suspicious, a TRACFIN report under Article L561-15 CMF. Screening evidence must be archived with the KYC file and refreshed at incorporation, upon a material UBO change, and no less frequently than every 12 months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI / Registre National des Entreprises) — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may include foreign-language words only if written in Latin characters and capable of being transliterated into French; French-language drafting of corporate instruments is required under the Toubon Law (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994). The name must not be contrary to public order or good morals, must not mislead the public, and must not create a likelihood of confusion with pre-existing company names or trademarks (Article R123-40 of the Commercial Code; Articles L711-2 and L711-4 of the Intellectual Property Code).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a pre-registration name reservation or extension mechanism for SAS entities: the RNE checks the requested dénomination sociale at the moment of filing the incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique. In case of rejection, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal notice; the appropriate remediation is to amend the draft articles and re-file a corrected dossier. Where rejection arises from a third-party trademark or passing-off objection, the applicant may institute infringement or interim measures proceedings before the competent Tribunal de commerce (summary référé) or, before formation is complete, request INPI's mediation support. No administrative appeal body handles company-name refusals, and no filing fee is refunded upon name-driven rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for a French SAS only through a duly accredited commercial domiciliation operator (Articles L123-11-2 and R123-166 et seq. of the French Commercial Code). The scheme must provide a physical French address, receipt of correspondence, and custody of corporate documents. A 'mailbox-only' arrangement without local managerial substance is incompatible with the ISIC 7320 cross-border survey SaaS business model and can trigger recharacterization of the registered office (siège social) and exposure to French permanent-establishment or corporate-residency assertions by DGFiP.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 3–5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection, principally triggered by URSSAF (social-security field controls), DGFiP tax audit triggers, or AML/CFT red flags. Routine on-site verification by RNE authorities is uncommon for low-risk ISIC 7320 activities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. for the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. and R.123-1 et seq. for business registration and the Registre National des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), acting as operator of the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises and custodian of the Registre National des Entreprises; the competent commercial court registry verifies commercial registration data.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of creation of a company (déclaration de création d'une société) submitted through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, accompanied by executed SAS articles of association and required beneficial ownership information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SAS; capital may be set at EUR 1 or a higher amount. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts before filing. Contributions in kind generally require an auditor unless a statutory exemption is validly elected.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company approve and adopt the articles of association in the form filed for incorporation and accept the subscription by each founding shareholder for the number and class of shares specified therein. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address], effective on registration. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed Président of the Société par Actions Simplifiée for an unlimited term, subject to the articles and applicable law, with authority to complete all incorporation, banking, tax, employment, and licensing formalities. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to execute all documents necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders and appointed French legal adviser; Guichet Unique submission portal operated by INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS articles in French, identifying shareholders, share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance powers, registered office, financial year, corporate purpose, and President. Execute the articles electronically or manually in counterparts. Obtain certified French translations for foreign-language supporting documents where required.
required_dossiers: Corporate shareholder extract and authorization, if applicable
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies, upload missing evidence, and resubmit through the Guichet Unique within the prescribed correction period. Maintain proof of submission and obtain a written clarification from the competent registry where the query is ambiguous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, notary, or Caisse des Dépôts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, provide the executed articles or draft articles, shareholder subscription schedule, identification documents, and beneficial ownership information. Transfer at least 50% of subscribed cash capital. Obtain the certificate of deposit and retain the transfer evidence for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Executed or near-final articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank compliance queries, replace deficient identification documents, or use a French notary or another authorized depositary. Do not represent the company as fully incorporated until registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized journal for legal notices (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a statutory formation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose summary, duration, President identity, and registration details. Pay the applicable fixed or word-based publication charge and obtain the certificate or attestation of publication for upload to the Guichet Unique.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or confirmed corporate particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any rejected wording with the legal-notice journal, republish if necessary, and upload the corrected attestation. Ensure the notice exactly matches the articles and electronic declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Electronic Incorporation and Beneficial Ownership Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises, operated by INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the company formalities file, select creation of a commercial company, complete the electronic declaration, upload the articles, capital certificate, legal-notice attestation, registered-office evidence, President declaration, identity documents, and beneficial ownership declaration. Electronically sign the filing, pay the applicable registry charges, and monitor the dashboard for queries.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate documents with legalization or apostille and translation, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the Guichet Unique to any registry request, correcting data rather than creating a duplicate filing. If the filing is rejected, request the stated legal or documentary basis, cure the defect, and resubmit or challenge the decision through the applicable registry or administrative review route.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI and the competent French tax administration (Service des Impôts des Entreprises); commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the registration extract and SIREN/SIRET identifiers, provide the registration evidence to the bank, convert the temporary capital account into the operating account, and activate tax and payroll accounts as applicable. Maintain the articles, registers, beneficial ownership record, share-transfer records, and annual accounts documentation.
required_dossiers: Payroll registration information, if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Escalate discrepancies in SIREN, SIRET, activity classification, or registered-office data to INPI and the competent registry. Amend incorrect information through the Guichet Unique and preserve the original filing history.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a consumer panel survey and market-research SaaS platform without manufacturing, controlled industrial activity, or regulated physical installations. Ordinary municipal and premises authorities remain competent for any leased office or physical facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating or manufacturing permit is ordinarily required for ISIC 7320 market research and a SaaS platform. Separate authorization may apply if the business later conducts regulated activities, operates public-facing premises, or processes specially regulated data.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale (MRAe), under the French environmental assessment framework administered by the Ministry for Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office and cloud-based SaaS operations; a screening or full assessment may arise only from a separate qualifying construction, land-use, infrastructure, or environmentally regulated project.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-emissions thresholds ordinarily apply to ordinary office operations. The company must prevent unlawful waste discharge, use authorized waste channels, segregate hazardous waste if generated, and comply with applicable municipal, building, waste, and environmental rules. Any data-center or physical installation is assessed separately under applicable environmental and classified-installation rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defense clearance is ordinarily required for a standard office. The occupier must comply with French fire-safety rules applicable to the premises, including emergency access, evacuation arrangements, fire equipment, and any required inspection documentation. Building-owner or landlord records should confirm structural suitability and load limits. The employer must complete workplace risk assessment, maintain the DUERP, provide occupational health arrangements, and implement workstation, electrical, accessibility, and emergency-safety controls.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – French General Directorate of Public Finances; online portal: impots.gouv.fr; professional portal: pro.impots.gouv.fr; sole incorporation filing gateway: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique operated by INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – File the SAS incorporation dossier (statuts, capital proof, non-resident director documentation) with the Guichet Unique via INPI. Step 2 – The French Trade and Companies Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) issues within the dossier authorization: (i) SIREN (9-digit national identifier), (ii) SIRET site-specific code, and (iii) INSEE APE code matching ISIC 7320/NAICS 541910. Step 3 – DGFiP automatically allocates the intra-community VAT number (n° TVA intracommunautaire) formatted as FR plus a 2-digit control key plus the SIREN, available in the company's DGFiP online tax account. Step 4 – For non-EU-resident parent shareholders, the SAS must appoint a resident tax representative (représentant fiscal) acceptable to DGFiP to receive tax correspondence, unless a French permanent establishment already exists. Step 5 – Validate French tax registration by obtaining the attestation d'immatriculation TVA from the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France applies entity-level corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) with no US-style check-the-box pass-through election. Available statutory election mechanisms: (i) Option for tax-consolidated group (régime d'intégration fiscale) under CGI Article 223A, permitting French subsidiaries controlled at least 95% maternally to pool taxable results (irrevocable five-year commitment, elected annually by the parent); (ii) Election to constitute a single taxable person for VAT (assujetti unique / groupe TVA) under CGI Article 256 C, effective since 1 January 2023; (iii) Election for the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) or non-EU IOSS regime for distance sales and B2C e-services; (iv) Tax-favorable options on IS amortization/depreciation (e.g., declining-balance depreciation, déduction des brevets) and the option for SARL's Irish-investment-type annuity regime which is not applicable to SAS; (v) Hybrid mismatch mandatory alignments under France's ATAD implementation (CGI Article 212 bis and Decree 2019-1558) require self-correction rather than elective neutralization, and no protective check-the-box exists for hybrid entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (value-added tax, VAT), governed by CGI Articles 256 through 289 and Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None for a French-established SAS – VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction irrespective of turnover level (CGI Article 286). For non-established EU sellers: distance sales threshold of EUR 35,000 per calendar year for France; for non-established non-EU suppliers of B2C e-services: EUR 10,000 EU-wide registration threshold under the OSS non-union regime. For a French SAS exporting services, the registration remains active as a permanent national VAT taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has adopted a compulsory structured electronic invoicing regime under Ordinance No. 2022-1290 and the 2024 Finance Act, with phased mandatory dates: from 1 September 2026, all taxable persons must be able to receive e-invoices and large enterprises and mid-cap companies (ETI) must issue e-invoices and transmit e-reporting data; from 1 September 2027, all other enterprises (including SMEs) must issue e-invoices and transmit e-reporting data. Mandatory formats: Factur-X (hybrid PDF/XML), UBL 2.1, or UN/CEFACT XML. Issuers must transmit through certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDP) or the State public portal (Portail Public de Facturation), which performs near-real-time data validation and forwards VAT-relevant transaction data to DGFiP. No physical or digital fiscal stamping (e-stamping) is required; the system is a clearance/validation and e-reporting mandate rather than a pre-approval per-invoice clearance regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For an ISIC 7320 market-research SaaS platform, French export zero-rating applies in two modes: (i) B2B services supplied to a customer established outside the EU qualify as 'outside the scope of French VAT' under CGI Article 259-1, as the place of supply is the recipient's establishment country; if supplied by the SAS, a 0% rate is applicable provided the supplier obtains the customer's foreign VAT registration number and demonstrable business-status evidence, and the service contract exists in writing with proof of delivery outside France. (ii) Physical goods exports (e.g., survey hardware panels or branded devices) qualify for zero-rating under CGI Article 262 (I) 1° only when goods physically leave the EU within 90 days of handover and are evidenced by customs export declarations. For B2C services supplied to non-EU individuals, the place of supply is the non-EU consumer's territory, hence exempt from French VAT; no input VAT recovery is conditioned on export documentation. Pure intra-EU B2B supply is reverse-charged on the EU acquirer under Article 283 and requires a valid EU VAT number without automatic zero-rating entitlement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAO – Déclaration Administrative Unique) transmitted via DELTA customs clearance system, bearing the MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank MT103/MT950 or SWIFT credit advice) evidencing foreign-currency payment settlement
Service contract (signed master agreement and statement of work) describing the market-research SaaS deliverables and offshore recipients
Performance deliverables: survey platform usage reports, dashboards, and IP delivery logs
Foreign customer's official VAT-ID (for B2B) or passport/official ID (for B2C) and certificate of business establishment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and Customs (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects) jointly audit export zero-rating claims. Failure to substantiate export within the statutory proof period triggers: (i) retroactive reversal of the zero-rated treatment, requiring the SAS to self-assess the 20% French VAT on the invoiced amounts; (ii) late-interest accrual at 0.20% per month (intérêts de retard, CGI Article 1727); (iii) negligence penalty of 40% (CGI Article 1729 a) or fraudulent misconduct penalty of 80% (CGI Article 1729 b), calculated on the evaded VAT; (iv) recovery of improperly claimed input VAT credits under CGI Articles 271-272 with and without good-faith shielding; (v) criminal exposure under Customs Code Article 414 for false export declarations, or under CGI Article 1741 for tax fraud, punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 500,000, plus suspension of business licenses; and (vi) clawback of export promotion subsidies and per-company publication on DGFiP's public sanctions list.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) acting as national central bank, balance-of-payments reporting authority, and operator of the TARGET2 component in France, in conjunction with the European Central Bank (ECB) for Eurosystem monetary policy. External financial relations and exchange-control policy are administered by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) under the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF), principally Articles L141-1 et seq., L151-1 et seq., and L561-1 et seq. Supervisory and enforcement authority for banking and payment institutions is allocated to the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), and financial-market conduct relating to FX and hedging instruments is supervised by the AMF (Autorité des Marchés Financiers). France, as a Eurozone Member State, applies no national exchange-control licensing system; capital and payment flows are governed by EU free-movement rules under TFEU Articles 63-66 supplemented by statistical declaration obligations enforced by Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is unconditionally and fully convertible in France for both current-account and capital-account transactions. No prior administrative authorisation or exchange-control permit is required for conversion of EUR into any foreign currency, for cross-border payment execution, or for repatriation of dividends, service fees, or liquidation proceeds. Current-account operations — including cross-border SaaS or market-research subscriptions, B2B survey-platform receivables, and mass disbursements to consumer panelists — are entirely free and may be settled in EUR or foreign currency without restriction. Capital-account operations are likewise liberalised. The only residual constraints are: (i) mandatory statistical balance-of-payments declarations to Banque de France, via its online reporting portal and pursuant to CMF Article L141-8 and DG Trésor implementing instructions, where aggregated cross-border settlements exceed EUR 750,000 per calendar month per counterparty country; and (ii) the EU/French foreign-direct-investment screening regime under CMF Articles L151-3 et seq., which applies only to investments into enumerated sensitive sectors (defence, dual-use, critical infrastructure, cybersecurity, and certain data/AI/health activities of strategic national interest) and is not engaged by a consumer-polling and market-research SaaS platform unless its data infrastructure is separately classified as critical. Profit remittance from the French SAS to non-resident shareholders is free of FX restriction. The sole tax hurdle is the statutory dividend withholding tax under Article 119 bis, 2 of the Code Général des Impôts: standard rate 25% for outbound dividends to non-French corporate shareholders, reducible or eliminable under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (minimum 5% participation and 24-month holding period) or under an applicable double-tax treaty; relief is obtained via the standard 'réclamation' procedure or reduced-withholding authorisation. Payments to foreign panel participants (survey incentives) are current-account transactions subject to zero FX-control barriers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no export-proceeds surrender regime whatsoever. There is no statutory requirement to repatriate, convert, or deposit foreign-currency export or service receipts into a French account, and no mandatory conversion ratio exists for EUR or foreign-currency earnings. The French SAS may lawfully retain survey-platform receivables in EUR or in foreign currency, indefinitely, in accounts held with a French credit institution or with a duly authorised electronic-money institution. The only enduring obligation is statistical: French residents must report cross-border settlements to Banque de France for balance-of-payments purposes (CMF Article L141-8, implementing EU statistical requirements). The reporting threshold is triggered where cumulative monthly settlements with non-residents exceed EUR 750,000 per counterparty country; the platform's service exports (ISIC 7320 consumer polling) must also be reflected in the annual 'liaison financière' declarations. No licence, permit, or prior approval attaches to the export of market-research services, and no conversion obligation applies to foreign-currency panel-payout funding.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué pour dépôt de capital) and Operational Account (compte courant professionnel)
Operational Account (compte professionnel) with EUR and multi-currency sub-accounts
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account; decentralised local decision-making favourable to SAS technology clients
Operational Account with multi-currency sweep structure for non-EU corridors

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High operational feasibility as a settlement and mass-payout layer, subject to defined legal constraints. Wise (Wise Payments SA, licensed as an electronic-money institution in Belgium by the NBB and passported into France) and Qonto (French digital bank, ACPR-licensed) are lawful options for daily treasury, supplier payments, panel rewards, and multi-currency disbursements. Feasibility rating: High for operational settlement and mass micro-payout automation (Wise Batch/API, PayPal Mass Payout funding); Low-Medium for capital escrow or as sole treasury bank. Legal constraints: (i) an EMI such as Wise is not a credit institution under Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 and may neither extend credit nor offer overdraft facilities; (ii) client funds held with Wise are safeguarded in segregated accounts at custodial banks, but are not covered by the French statutory deposit-guarantee scheme (FGDR) — the platform should therefore cap balances at operational-cycle needs; (iii) a fully licensed French digital bank such as Qonto may offer credit products, but core liquidity and borrowing lines (Bpifrance co-financing, commercial overdraft) are more advantageously priced at a Tier-1 bank; (iv) Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declarations are executed through tier-1 credit institutions, not EMIs, requiring the SAS to retain at least one licensed bank account for compliance reporting; (v) capital injections and equity contributions must flow through a licensed credit institution under wire-traceability rules, never through an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a mandatory physical-presence requirement for corporate account opening. ACPR guidance, implementing the EU Anti-Money-Laundering framework (CMF Articles L561-5 et seq.), permits risk-based customer due diligence using eIDAS-compliant electronic identification, video-verification, and certified identity providers. In practice: fintechs such as Qonto and Wise allow fully remote onboarding in 1-5 business days; Tier-1 banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole, BPCE) generally require at least one interview — by videoconference or in branch — with the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and may require a power of attorney for secondary signatories. Typical Tier-1 onboarding timeline is 3-8 weeks, conditioned on delivery of the Kbis extract (evidencing RCS registration and SIREN/SIRET identifiers), articles of association, UBO register (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), FATCA/CRS self-certifications, projected-transaction volumes, and a commercial narrative for mass panel payouts. For an ISIC 7320 platform holding no statutory licence, the banking-compliance gate is moderate; the main issue is not regulatory permission but bank-specific risk appetite for high-volume micro-disbursements to retail panelists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency B2B-to-retail flow mismatch: onboarding analyst suspects layering where large cross-border SWIFT inflows from corporate clients are followed by mass micro-disbursements (EUR 1-50) to foreign individuals, potentially screened as a money-mule network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business-model memorandum citing ISIC 7320 classification and platform commercial documentation; panel-participant enrolment workflows with identity-verification logs and geo-tagging; signed survey-reward terms of service with payout thresholds; statistical ratio of panel remuneration to survey activity per jurisdiction; 12-month projected transaction volumes by country; commercial agreements with subscribing corporate clients; source-of-funds evidence for major B2B receivables; transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening policy documentation; TRACFIN-relevant risk-assessment matrix; board resolution approving the payout model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity through non-resident or trust-based ownership chains: where the SAS is ultimately held by non-EU shareholders, enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered and the bank requests source-of-wealth evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified formation documents of each entity up the ownership chain (articles, registry extracts or equivalent, apostilled where necessary); group structure chart showing the natural-person UBOs; RCS-filed UBO declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs); certified identity documents and proof-of-address for UBOs; source-of-wealth statement for the capital injection with supporting bank references; audited consolidated accounts of the ultimate parent; sworn French translation of all non-French documents to avoid rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment routing: clients or group treasuries propose settling through a third party (group treasury, payment service provider, or strategic partner), which triggers source-of-funds verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written third-party payment authorisation agreement establishing commercial purpose; chain-of-title evidence for each third-party settlement (underlying invoice, contract, transaction audit trail); KYB/KYC package for the third party (incorporation certificate, UBO register, director identification); board resolution of the SAS approving the routing arrangement; legal opinion confirming compliance with CMF Articles L561-10 et seq. and Regulation (EU) 2015/847 originator-information rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Jurisdictional concentration and sanctions-adjacent exposure: panel rewards originating from or destined to high-risk or restricted territories may trigger extended sanctions screening and potential account restrictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GDPR-compliant anonymised participant geo-distribution report; sanctions-screening software logs evidencing negative-match results; country-risk matrix prepared by a compliance consultant; confirmation that the platform does not onboard participants from EU-restrictive-measures jurisdictions; evidence of any required special approvals from Direction Générale du Trésor; board-approved restricted-country policy and weekly screening cadence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing for share capital, equity contributions, and strategic financing: (a) EU/EEA shareholder wires — SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 pain.001 messages with purpose code 'GMTO' in the <PURP> tag and a 70-char remittance reference 'AUGMENTATION DE CAPITAL FR_SAS'; funds must be credited to a dedicated blocked account (compte bloqué) at a French credit institution or notary, which will issue the statutory attestation de dépôt des fonds for registration of the capital increase with the RCS (greffe du tribunal de commerce). (b) Non-EU/EEA shareholder wires — SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for bank-to-bank instructions) with a complete originator-information block per Regulation (EU) 2015/847 and an ISO 20022 purpose code appropriate to capital subscription (e.g., 'CAPH' or 'FXCK' for monetary capital contributions as instructed by the receiving bank); the receiving bank will require the shareholders' resolution, subscription form, board minutes, and the notarial or banking deposit attestation. No prior FX-authorisation applies. For inbound flows above EUR 750,000 per calendar month per counterparty country, the receiving bank will submit the mandatory Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration using the capital-contribution purpose code from the Banque de France reporting manual; the SAS must corroborate the economic substance of the contribution with its Kbis extract, UBO registry, and shareholder source-of-funds documentation. If capital arrives from offshore trust structures, enhanced EDD is triggered, including potential TRACFIN reporting only where red flags persist. Third-party payment processors (PayPal HoldCo, Wise) are not acceptable channels for equity capital or shareholder loans and must never receive inbound capital injectiows; such flows must be settled through a licensed bank to preserve legal validity of the capital increase and to protect the limitation-of-liability shield of the SAS.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Select the clearing rail by beneficiary geography and purpose: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) for all EU/EEA panel payouts and supplier payments, ideally batched as ISO 20022 XML files (pain.001.001.09) via host-to-host banking or via Wise's SEPA gateway; SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) is available for payouts up to EUR 100,000 requiring near-real-time credit. (b) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA customer credit transfers, covering USD, GBP, CHF, and local-currency payouts; each MT103 must include full originator and beneficiary data under Regulation (EU) 2015/847 and a legitimate purpose code (e.g., 'BENEF' for beneficiary-only transfers or 'CASH' for ordinary payments) as instructed by the UK/European correspondent bank; Fx conversion can be performed at the platform's Tier-1 bank or at the beneficiary bank depending on cost. (c) PayPal Mass Payout API for micro-incentives to consumer panelists; funds are held in the platform's PayPal commercial account and settled against the payer's Master Transaction List (MTL) on a T+1 cycle, with the source funding drawn from the Tier-1 operational account; PayPal is a regulated payment institution, not a bank, so cash balances above payout-cycle requirements should be swept daily back to the bank. (d) Wise Platform (API) serves as the secondary rail for low-cost cross-border payouts in non-EU jurisdictions, operating under its Belgian EMI licence and safeguarding client funds in segregated accounts at custodian banks; the French SAS must maintain the main treasury at a Tier-1 bank, using Wise only for optimisation of conversion spreads and reach. (e) Commercial Letters of Credit are generally unsuitable for service-based micro-disbursements under ISIC 7320; where a large corporate client insists on trade-based security, an irrevocable at-sight documentary credit issued by SWIFT (MT700) and advised or confirmed by the French bank is permissible, but the platform should default to open-account settlement with wire transfer for cost efficiency. All outbound disbursements must be mapped to an internal payment-ID and survey-incentive ledger to demonstrate traceability and auditability; treasury policy should maintain EUR operating balances equal to at least one full quarter of operating expenses, with USD/GBP buffers capped at three months of expected panel-payout requirements and swept or hedged as per the instruments below.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forward (change à terme) — OTC with a Tier-1 French credit institution under the FBF (French Banking Federation) master agreement for spot and forward FX; maturities 1-24 months; no AMF authorisation required for the end-user when used purely for hedging.

FX options (European-style plain vanilla calls and puts) on EUR/USD and EUR/GBP — OTC through licensed banks or MiFID-authorised brokers; appropriate for downside protection on fixed USD panel-reward budgets.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for restricted or low-liquidity emerging-market currencies — available OTC via Paris-based global bank desks; settled in EUR against a standard fixing source (WM/Reuters); documented under an ISDA 2002 French-law master agreement with a credit-support annex.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD fixed-float and basis swaps) — permissible for tenor-matched alignment of injected USD equity with EUR operating expenditures when capital is held offshore; governed by standard ISDA/CSA documentation.
FX swap (swap de change) — permitted for short-term liquidity rolling between EUR and USD or GBP to optimise payout-currency positions without incurring open FX exposure.
FX spot (change au comptant) — unrestricted and available for daily operational conversions via the Tier-1 bank or a licensed FX broker.
Listed currency futures and exchange-traded options on EUR/USD — permitted through a MiFID-authorised French broker; economically practical only for notional positions above EUR 500,000 per contract.

The SAS must confine all derivative activity to genuine economic exposure hedging; speculative open positions would constitute regulated investment services and would require AMF licensing, which is outside the permitted treasury operating model.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit (financial statements, annexes and management report) — dépôt des comptes annuels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Commercial Court Registry), filed via the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting approval by 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year end; statutory deposit within one month of approval, i.e. by 31 July; maximum seven months after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial-court injunction (injonction de faire) with daily coercive penalty (astreinte); risk of RCS administrative strike-off after formal notice where the entity appears inactive; legal representatives exposed to criminal fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration de résultats, form 2065, with annexes 2050 et seq.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year fiscal year end: due 3 May of the following year for online filers (postponed to the next business day if a weekend or public holiday); non-calendar fiscal year end: within three months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ten per cent assessment penalty (reduced to five per cent if regularized within 30 days of the first notice) plus statutory monthly late-payment interest; d'office tax assessment where the return remains omitted after a second demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner declaration updates (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs — DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique, incorporated in the RCS corporate file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any event changing beneficial ownership — e.g. share transfer crossing the 25 per cent threshold, change of controlling shareholder or new direct ownership structure; where data is unchanged, no separate annual filing is required, but the accuracy is re-confirmed at each annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 10,000 for non-filing or false statements; Guichet Unique blocks subsequent registry formalities until the declaration is regularized

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder collective decision approving the financial statements and appropriation of profit (AGM or written resolution per SAS bylaws)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal statutory minute book; approval documented and evidenced to the Greffe before the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the fiscal year end (30 June for a 31 December year end); commercial-court extension available in exceptional circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accounts cannot be lawfully deposited and no dividend may be distributed without approved accounts; protracted delay triggers shareholder legal action and management liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) where the SAS exceeds two of three criteria: total balance-sheet assets EUR 6,000,000; net turnover EUR 12,000,000; 50 average employees. Appointment is also compulsory where required by the SAS bylaws or by group-law/consolidation rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) under the French Commercial Code for the individual statutory accounts; IFRS permitted only for consolidated financial statements of groups whose securities are admitted to trading

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The DBE is filed at registration and re-filed via Guichet Unique within 30 days of any transfer exceeding 25 per cent of share capital or voting rights, any change of actual control, or any change in the identity/coordinates of a declared beneficial owner. At each annual accounts deposit the legal representative confirms that the RCS and beneficial-owner data remain accurate; French law does not impose a standalone annual UBO return, but material non-updates at the annual filing are treated as non-compliance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share-transfer ledger (registre des mouvements de titres)
Minute book of shareholder resolutions (registre des décisions et procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 130–650 per annum (EUR 10–50 per month) for INSEE-approved commercial domiciliation services and corporate-secretarial handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500–16,500 per annum (EUR 5,000–15,000) where the compulsory audit thresholds are met; no statutory audit fee is legally incurred while the SAS remains below the thresholds and no voluntary auditor is appointed

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. Eligible small and medium-sized companies may qualify for a 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the statutory share-capital, ownership, and turnover conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Potential incentives include the qualifying SME reduced rate, research and development tax credit (Crédit d'impôt recherche), and innovation tax credit for eligible expenditure and activities. Eligibility is fact-specific; no general tax holiday applies to a consumer-panel survey platform. The standard social contribution on corporate income tax may also apply to companies meeting the statutory revenue and tax thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return) and its schedules, filed electronically through the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) professional tax portal or through an authorized electronic filing provider. Form 2572 is used for the corporate income tax balance payment; Form 2571 is used for installments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; corporate income tax installments are generally paid quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the statutory deadline is the second working day following 1 May, subject to the DGFiP electronic-filing calendar and any officially announced extension. The corporate income tax balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end; for a calendar-year company, by 15 May. Installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to statutory exceptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS's legal name, SIREN number, registered office, principal activity, financial year dates, and applicable tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SAS files as a French-resident corporate taxpayer and reports its French tax identification details. Foreign ownership does not, by itself, change the filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, tax regime and return status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the corporate income tax regime and whether the filing is an original, amended, or final return, as applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A SAS is ordinarily subject to corporate income tax at entity level. Do not use a non-resident company's branch-return treatment for the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable result determined from statutory accounts after tax adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, exempt or separately taxed income, and applicable tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French tax rules to the SAS's worldwide taxable profits, subject to applicable treaty provisions and specific source or exemption rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute tax at the applicable rate, claim eligible reduced rates or credits, and reconcile installments and other payments against the tax due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder cannot claim the SAS's corporate tax credits personally. The SAS must retain evidence supporting any incentive or credit claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete applicable disclosures concerning related-party transactions, tax groups, and other required schedules; submit transfer-pricing forms where statutory thresholds or reporting rules apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose cross-border related-party dealings accurately. French transfer-pricing documentation and transaction-reporting obligations can apply to a French subsidiary of a foreign group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare and pay the final corporate income tax balance after crediting installments and eligible tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is made by the French taxpayer through the prescribed electronic payment system; a foreign parent does not replace the SAS as the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare and pay applicable quarterly corporate income tax installments, subject to statutory exemptions and thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess installment obligations using the SAS's preceding tax liabilities and current-year statutory rules; document any exemption relied upon.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, which may rise to 40% after a formal notice is not remedied within the statutory period and to 80% in cases such as undisclosed activity or abuse of rights. Late payment generally incurs a 5% surcharge plus late interest, currently 0.20% per month, subject to statutory adjustments or relief. Inaccurate or incomplete returns may attract additional penalties, including a 40% penalty for deliberate breach and 80% for fraudulent conduct or certain abusive arrangements. Penalties depend on the facts and applicable procedural rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The domestic withholding rate on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally 25%, subject to treaty relief, applicable European Union rules, and statutory exemptions. A qualifying EU parent may obtain an exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, subject to ownership, holding-period, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the payer with the applicable French treaty-relief certificate, generally Form 5000 (residence certificate) and, where required, the relevant income-specific Form 5001 or other prescribed documentation. The certificate must be certified by the recipient's tax authority and supplied within the required period. If relief is not applied at source, the recipient may generally seek a refund through the prescribed French procedure, supported by proof of residence, beneficial ownership, payment, and tax withheld. Confirm the applicable treaty article, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose test provisions, and current DGFiP instructions before payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are generally subject to French withholding under domestic rules, commonly at the applicable corporate income tax rate, with treaty reductions or exemptions potentially available. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding tax, except for statutory exceptions, including payments to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions and certain interest-like payments. Treaty rates and exemptions vary by recipient, beneficial ownership, payment characterization, and treaty; European Union directives may apply where their conditions are met. Obtain and retain valid residence and beneficial-ownership documentation before applying relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: French full transfer-pricing documentation under Article L.13 AA of the Tax Procedures Code generally applies where the French entity's annual turnover excluding tax or gross assets is at least EUR 150 million, or where it belongs to a group meeting the statutory threshold through another qualifying entity. A separate annual transfer-pricing declaration (Form 2257-SD) generally applies at the EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold, including specified group relationships. Thresholds and scope should be checked against current law and the entity's group facts.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. French substance remains relevant under transfer-pricing rules, permanent-establishment analysis, beneficial-ownership requirements, anti-abuse doctrines, controlled foreign company rules, and treaty principal-purpose tests. The SAS should maintain personnel, decision-making, functions, assets, and risk-control evidence consistent with its claimed income and contractual arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Incorrect corporate income tax return or omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting taxable income, claiming unsupported deductions or credits, failing to file, or materially misstating the tax position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late interest, and surcharges that may reach 40% for deliberate breach or 80% for fraud or specified abusive conduct; criminal penalties may apply to tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face criminal liability for personal participation in tax fraud and, in qualifying circumstances, personal tax-debt liability under statutory procedures. Corporate limited liability is not a defense to an individual's own offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party services, licenses, financing, or other transactions outside the arm's-length principle; failing to maintain required documentation or submit required disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustments, tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Failure to provide required documentation may trigger a penalty of the greater of EUR 10,000 or 5% of transfer-pricing adjustments, subject to statutory conditions and caps.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal criminal or civil exposure for intentional misconduct, false records, or participation in fraud; ordinary company-level reassessments do not automatically pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits contrary to company law, applying treaty relief without valid entitlement or documentation, or failing to withhold and remit tax when required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of withholding tax, late interest, and applicable surcharges; unlawful distributions may also be subject to restitution and company-law remedies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable where statutory conditions for personal liability are met, including serious and repeated tax non-compliance or intentional participation. A dividend recipient may also be required to repay an unlawful distribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, fictitious services, or tax fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or using sham invoices, concealing revenue, fabricating survey or SaaS costs, or knowingly arranging transactions to evade tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, substantial tax penalties, and potential criminal prosecution. Tax fraud may be punished by imprisonment and fines under the French Tax Code and Penal Code, with higher sanctions for aggravated circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who direct, authorize, or knowingly assist fraud may face personal criminal fines and imprisonment. Asset recovery or confiscation may apply where legally authorized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fictitious residence, shell arrangements, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming treaty residence, beneficial ownership, or an exemption through an entity lacking the relevant entitlement or using an arrangement principally to obtain an improper tax benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or statutory relief, reassessment, interest, and penalties under domestic anti-abuse rules and applicable treaty provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal exposure depends on participation, intent, and statutory grounds. A foreign shareholder's ownership alone does not establish director liability or pierce the SAS's limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly processing criminal proceeds, concealing beneficial ownership, or making prohibited payments to sanctioned persons or jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal and administrative sanctions may include substantial fines, imprisonment, asset seizure, and restrictions on business activity, depending on the offense and applicable sanctions regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and other individuals who knowingly participate may be prosecuted personally. Travel restrictions or asset freezes may be imposed only under applicable legal procedures; they are not automatic consequences of a tax filing breach.
